currentGap: The fixed commercial bar still wins on authored environmental and asset finish. New map storage, specimen displays and finer brass/iron/enamel finishes are in scratch review. The real state worker passed the completed-body/main-thread-stall regression; remaining native acceptance is running.

rounds.label: BASELINE
rounds.title: The existing physical room
rounds.summary: The working autonomous engine is retained. The initial visual review found a primitive room, a tiny probe, flat mechanisms and weak focal lighting.
rounds.gap: Crafted architecture, a developed protagonist and tactile mechanisms.

rounds.label: ITERATION 01
rounds.title: The archive takes shape
rounds.summary: A furnished archive, physical materials, an articulated archivist and a game-focused interface are now rendered. An independent critic inspected the actual captures.
rounds.gap: The central lock still reads as a ring on a blank door. Repetitive shiny wood and limited shadowing remain visible.

rounds.label: ITERATION 02
rounds.title: Physical mechanisms and a real escape
rounds.summary: All eight mechanism families now contain moving parts; the vault opens onto a passage. Real screenshots received another independent comparison with the fixed commercial reference.
rounds.gap: Nested rings still dominate the hero lock; character close-up was clipped, and portrait room framing was too distant. These findings are driving the next iteration.

rounds.label: ITERATION 03
rounds.title: Crafted vault, developed Archivist
rounds.summary: The vault now has meshing gears, connected drawbars and guided bolts. A complete character portrait, stronger portrait scene framing, furniture detail and a real exit passage are captured from the running renderer. A fresh chronology-blinded A/B critic preferred this build over baseline in every view and accepted the developed character; the separate commercial benchmark still wins.
rounds.gap: Repeated furniture silhouettes and staging, a clipped overview character, and the hard hover cone remain visible.

rounds.label: ITERATION 04
rounds.title: Constructed furniture and complete staging
rounds.summary: A shaped writing bench, upholstered chair, differentiated instrument stands and bookcase crowns are now visible. The overview keeps the whole Archivist in frame; confirmed escape stages the character at the open doorway. A fresh blind critic preferred this pass in four views, with the unchanged mechanism tied.
rounds.gap: Broad fill light, weak contact grounding and repeated wood/gold surface treatment still fall behind the fixed commercial reference.

rounds.label: ITERATION 05
rounds.title: Grounded materials and complete inspection
rounds.summary: Baked contact lighting, corrected timber scale and a diffuse ceiling give the room depth. Shared stable-object submissions preserve geometry while reducing the opening capture from 171 to 112 calls. The complete mechanism now fits clear of the interface in oblique desktop and phone views. Independent image critics accept these improvements; the fixed reference still wins on authored room and asset finish.
rounds.gap: Sparse repetitive room dressing, coarse hardware finish and the plain exit reveal remain. A network observer candidate was rejected by native evidence; its dedicated-worker replacement is undergoing acceptance.

checks: All 102 Game 8 unit and contract tests pass after lighting, batching, inspection, sealed exit and worker integration. The worker-inclusive stream self-test also passes.

A genuine worker response finished parsing during a 2,600 ms main-thread stall and was delivered after the former timeout without aborting. Remaining native timeout, recovery, live desktop and full-room budget checks are in progress.

Native evidence rejected the earlier Resource Timing observer candidate despite passing synthetic tests. Its failed probes remain alongside the dedicated-worker replacement; an unsupported CDP fault-injection command is recorded as a harness failure, not a product pass.

Round 05 actual low-tier stills: opening 112 draw calls / 115,832 triangles; confirmed escape 120 / 118,316. These images precede the sealed-jamb and worker changes. Still captures do not establish FPS.
The active circular vault mechanism is independently accepted in oblique desktop and 390-pixel phone views. The whole casing and tiny mobile markings remain qualified.

Exact eleven/twelve-puzzle geometry tests reduce dynamic submissions from 165/179 to 77/81 before the small jamb addition, with unchanged triangles. Larger combined bounds can submit more offscreen geometry in closeups; the full live budget gate remains open.
The real autonomous capture run escaped at tick 25 with all eight puzzles solved and no captured browser console/page errors.

Historical browser evidence: nine scenarios passed at Round 03; a separate Round 04 resource test passed all 65 real frames across four themes. These are separate source checkpoints, not one current green run.
Historical raw-buffer cleanup held 348 outstanding buffers across six cycles. Renderer teardown retired one context while a surviving renderer kept shared assets and continued drawing.
The original desktop fixed-700 ms check failed. Its replacement waits for actual public state advancement and matching UI; the existing 190-call and 150,000-triangle limits remain unchanged.
The new lighting wins its concealed-source predecessor comparison; The Room 4 wins the separate concealed-source commercial comparison. Visual parity has not been established.
Character batching preserves 12,526 triangles and all sampled articulation while reducing mesh submissions from 61 to 39.
